title: OpenProposal constructors
description: Stage 4 input: kernel/constructors.yaml. Each constructor (type rules § 7) is a template that exists only in the model. Its shell is the schema of one concrete copy, written with JSON Schema 2020-12 keywords, where every type position is a slot that holds a model type. The emitter publishes one named copy per use by filling the slots; List and Map are filled in place. Spec sources are quoted and digested, so a constructor goes stale when a row it rests on changes.

constructors.description: The templates. A spec whose text uses none, as AdCOM's lists, binds each one absent, so its kernel holds none.

parts.description: The named types that a shell references and that don't depend on a parameter, apart from primitives (type rules § 7). They are in the constructor layer, so they reference only primitives, and every copy shares them.

description.description: The published description of every copy: what a value means, for someone who receives a payload.

fallback.description: The bare value that may stand in for the full form (type rules § 8). When a use supplies the parameter, the copy is `anyOf` the bare value and the full form, under the fallback's name; without it, the copy is the full form only.

parameter.description: An optional parameter that the shell doesn't use.

suffix.description: Appended to the full form's name to name the union.

statement.description: The IR statement that allows the bare value. It is one of the constructor's spec sources.

decision.description: The decision record behind the bare value's type, which the specification doesn't state.

rules.description: Rules on a copy that JSON Schema can't express (type rules § 9). The schema accepts every vector of a rule; the rule rejects the invalid ones.

vectors.description: Values that a copy, made with the given arguments, must accept and must reject. Each block makes one copy.

kept.description: Why the constructor stays though no mapping entry, and no template an entry applies, applies it on any lock. Without it, every constructor is applied on some lock.

decision.description: The decision record that says why the constructor stays.

reason.description: Why it stays, in one sentence.

concept.description: The concept of `kernel/domains.yaml` the part represents: the concept's type, or one of its components.

decisions.description: The decision records behind the members and constraints the sources don't state, one for each, each on the locks it lists, where the sources state it on the others; without `locks`, on every lock.

rules.description: Rules on a value of the part that JSON Schema can't express (type rules § 9). The schema accepts every vector of a rule; the rule rejects the invalid ones.

vectors.description: Values the part must accept and must reject.

accepts.description: What an argument may be. `any`: any property type. `named`: a named type, or a copy of a constructor that has a name, so a list or a map never holds an inline form (type rules § 4). `string`: a named type whose values are strings, as a JSON object key is. `ordered`: a primitive whose values are ordered, a number or a date-time. `unordered`: a named type or copy that isn't an ordered primitive. `closed`: a named type or copy whose values aren't objects, or are objects that reject the members they don't name.

names.description: The parameter whose options this one names, as `included[]` and the `pricing` keys name the options of `available[]`: its argument is that parameter's argument where the option is a string, named by its value, and `Uuid`, the option's `id`, where the option is an object (D-007).

carries.description: The member an object option carries, typed by this parameter's argument and required, where the parameter names the options of `names` and the option is an object: an object option carries its `id`, which `included[]` and the `pricing` keys name it by (D-046). The model gives the member to each object type that is an option, so the mapping keeps the members the specification writes.

decision.description: The decision that gives every object option the member.

departure.description: The decision that gives the member to an option whose members the specification lists without it, a closed object, which departs from what the text settles; an open option, whose members the text doesn't state, rests on `decision` alone.

naming.description: How a copy is named (type rules § 7). `field`: the field that uses it, in PascalCase, plus the suffix. `argument`: the named argument for `parameter`, plus the suffix. `inline`: the copy is emitted in place and has no name.

shell.description: The schema of a copy: an object, an array, or an untagged union. Only these keywords occur, so a copy can't carry a constraint beside a reference, an inline object, `allOf`, `oneOf`, or a keyword outside 2020-12.

additionalProperties.description: `false` for an object with fixed members, or a slot for the values of a map.

dependentSchemas.description: A condition that holds when a member is present, such as "`allowed` stands alone".

if.description: A value of one member that the part rejects, with `then: false`, such as a daypart window's `start` of `24:00`: a constraint that belongs to one member of the part stays in the part (type rules § 4).

type.description: `object`, so a value of another JSON type doesn't meet the condition, and only `type` rejects it.

unionShell.description: An untagged union, which type rules § 8 allows only for the forms draft 1 requires.

assertion.description: A condition on how many members are present.

listSlot.description: A slot that holds a list, with bounds on its items: a constraint that belongs to one member of a part stays in the part (type rules § 4), as a daypart window's `days` holds at least one day, each once. The list is filled in place, so the bounds sit on the list itself, where JSON Schema and every generator read them.

slot.description: A type position. The emitter replaces it with a reference to a named type or a copy, or with an inline list or map. Only `description` may sit beside it (type rules § 5).

arguments.description: The copy the vectors are checked against: one type per parameter.

id.description: `constructor:<constructor>:<token>`. The constructor is the rule's owner, so every copy carries the rule.

source.description: Where the rule comes from (type rules § 9): specification elements, quoted and digested, or the decision record behind it.

id.description: `kernel:<part>:<token>`. The part is the rule's owner.

sources.description: Where the constructor comes from. `spec` is required: every constructor cites the rows that define it.

spec.description: Specification elements, quoted and digested as `npm run cite` prints them.

name.description: A model type or parameter name.
